---
title: "Summary · Composing Hello Pico on Kubernetes"
---

## Key takeaways

- **Crossplane** extends a Kubernetes control plane with the ability to
  author your own higher-level, composable APIs and have the cluster
  produce the concrete resources they imply.
- The Crossplane primitives introduced in this lesson are **Provider**,
  **XRD**, **Composition**, **Composite Resource (XR)**, and
  **Managed Resource** — all defined in the
  [Glossary](../../glossary.qmd).
- The Crossplane path maps cleanly onto the Pico pipeline:
  **Rules ↔ XR**, **Parser ↔ XRD**, **Composer ↔ Composition**,
  **Pico artifact ↔ Managed Resources on the cluster**.
- The **reference target environment** for the follow-on runnable lab
  is **local minikube** — small enough for a laptop, full enough to
  host a real Kubernetes control plane.
- The Crossplane [Lab](lab.qmd) for this lesson is the reusable
  [Hello Pico on Kubernetes](../../../../labs/hello-pico-on-kubernetes/index.html)
  lab. It installs Crossplane on a local minikube cluster, declares an
  `XHelloWorldPico` XRD and its Composition, and reconciles a single
  Composite Resource into a Kubernetes `Job` that prints
  `Hello, Pico!` — a full end-to-end runnable exercise of the
  Rules ↔ XR / Parser ↔ XRD / Composer ↔ Composition /
  Pico ↔ Managed Resources mapping.

## What comes next

- **Part 2 — Composing Hello Pico** will develop the Composition side of
  the story once Part 1 is fully in place. See
  [Part 2](../../part-2/index.qmd).
- **Part 3 — Extending the composition** will layer additional Managed
  Resources on top of the base composition. See
  [Part 3](../../part-3/index.qmd).
- The reusable Hello Pico on Kubernetes lab is now runnable end to
  end on local minikube. See the lab's
  [Objectives](../../../../labs/hello-pico-on-kubernetes/objectives.html)
  page for the exact tool version pins used to verify it.
